mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the current month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite persistent FEDFUNDS > 5.25% for 4 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum measured by PAYEMS triggers increased consumer confidence and corporate hiring intentions, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% from the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are flat or negative when PAYEMS growth exceeds +2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 110 indicates weakening supply-side demand, which amplifies risk premia and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from the prior 5-day average when INDPRO crosses below 110 from above.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals sticky inflation expectations that push the Fed toward tighter policy, which depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite CPIAUCSL monthly change > +0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining unemployment (UNRATE) and rising retail sales (HOUST) jointly indicate a labor market recovery that supports equity valuations, producing positive 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: labor market improving alongside retail activity
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when both UNRATE is falling and HOUST is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) below 130,000 suggests a cooling labor market, which raises uncertainty and lowers S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative when PAYEMS falls below 130,000.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 5%, it signals a shift toward accommodative policy, which tends to boost equity valuations and drive positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite 3-month SMA(FEDFUNDS) > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates structural supply constraints, which elevates risk premia and produces negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month's value for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative when INDPRO shows no sustained decline over 3 months.
